\[
\hat{P}^{\text{hard}} = T_{3D}^{-1}\!\left(\gamma(T_{3D}(\mathbf{P}))\right),
\qquad
\hat{P}^{\text{wien}} = T_{3D}^{-1}\!\left(\omega \cdot T_{3D}(\mathbf{P})\right),
\quad
\omega = \frac{\lvert T_{3D}(\mathbf{B}) \rvert^2}{\lvert T_{3D}(\mathbf{B}) \rvert^2 + \sigma^2}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\mathbf{P}\): A 3D group of similar noisy patches
- \(\mathbf{B}\): The same group from the basic estimate
- \(T_{3D}\): The orthonormal 3D DCT
- \(\gamma\): The hard threshold at 2.7 sigma
- \(\omega\): The empirical Wiener coefficients
- \(\sigma\): The noise standard deviation

P is a 3D group: patches of 8 x 8 pixels similar to a reference patch, stacked. T_3D is the orthonormal 3D DCT. In the first step, gamma sets every coefficient with |x| <= 2.7 sigma to 0. Similar patches share their structure, so the stack's signal gathers in a few large coefficients while the noise spreads over all of them. In the second step, B is the same group taken from the basic estimate, and omega is an empirical Wiener filter. Every patch estimate is put back in place and averaged with a weight that favors groups with less left after filtering.
